summary: You were in the hospital because your heart was holding on to extra fluid. Your heartbeat was fast, and you had a skin infection on your right leg. Your water pill changed from furosemide to torsemide, and your metoprolol is now a once-a-day kind. Weigh yourself every day and finish the antibiotic. Never take both water pills.

diagnoses.plain: Heart failure where the heart is stiff and holds on to fluid
diagnoses.clinical: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, resolved

diagnoses.plain: Skin infection on the right lower leg

new.name: Torsemide
new.why: Your new water pill. It replaces furosemide and takes extra fluid off. You will urinate more.

new.name: Metoprolol succinate
new.why: A long-acting version that keeps your heart rate steady. It replaces the old short-acting metoprolol.

new.name: Cephalexin
new.howOften: four times a day for 4 more days
new.why: An antibiotic to finish treating the leg infection. Take every dose.

continue.name: Apixaban
continue.howOften: twice a day, as on your final medication list
continue.why: A blood thinner that prevents strokes from the irregular heartbeat. Never stop it without asking your doctor.

continue.name: Atorvastatin
continue.why: Lowers cholesterol to protect your heart.

continue.name: Home diabetes regimen
continue.howOften: as on your final medication list

stop.name: Furosemide
stop.why: Stopped. Torsemide replaces it. Do not take both water pills.

stop.name: Previous short-acting metoprolol regimen
stop.why: Stopped. The new once-a-day metoprolol succinate replaces it.

checklist.text: Take Torsemide 20 mg once a day. Do not take furosemide anymore
Take Metoprolol succinate 75 mg once a day. Do not take the old metoprolol
Take Cephalexin 500 mg four times a day until it is gone
Take Empagliflozin 10 mg once a day
Take Apixaban 5 mg twice a day, every day
Weigh yourself every day and write it down
Look at your right leg every day: redness, warmth and swelling should be shrinking
Get your kidney and electrolyte blood tests as ordered after the water pill change
Put your right leg up when resting

call911: Severe or quickly worsening shortness of breath
goToER: A fast or irregular heartbeat that does not settle and makes you feel unwell
Swelling or weight going up quickly
The leg redness spreading past the marked line, or the pain getting much worse fast
Heavy bleeding while on the blood thinner
callClinic: Dizziness or blood pressure changes, so we can check your fall risk
Any new drainage from the leg

followUps.why: Check your heart rate, fluid and the new medicines
Check the leg infection and your blood tests

questionsToAsk: How much weight gain should make me call you?
What should I do if I accidentally take furosemide and torsemide on the same day?
When will the leg redness be fully gone?
Do I need to change my apixaban dose?
When are my blood tests due?
